mainTitle: 🔒 Privacy Violations: The Systemic LGPD Violation
mainDescription: Detailed analysis of LGPD violations and the right to privacy — This article examines the systematic violations of the privacy of user WazzimaGiygg (Pedro Henrique Cardona Peres) by Lusophone Wikipedia administrators and checkusers, including doxxing, data collection without consent, device fingerprinting, illegal data retention and multiple violations of the General Data Protection Law (LGPD).
section1Title: 1. Introduction: Privacy as a Fundamental Right
section1Text1: Privacy is a fundamental right protected by the Federal Constitution (Art. 5, X), the General Data Protection Law (LGPD - Law 13.709/2018) and the Marco Civil da Internet (Law 12.965/2014). In the WazzimaGiygg case, this right was systematically violated by Lusophone Wikipedia administrators and checkusers, who treated the user's personal data without consent, with deviation of purpose and with vexatious public exposure.

objective2: • Analyze doxxing and public exposure of personal data

warningLgpdText: The WazzimaGiygg case reveals multiple LGPD violations, including data processing without consent, deviation of purpose, lack of transparency, public exposure of personal data and illegal data retention. Penalties can reach R$ 50 million per violation.
sub2_1Text1: Art. 6 of the LGPD establishes the fundamental principles that must govern the processing of personal data. All were violated in the WazzimaGiygg case:

sub2_2Text1: Art. 7 of the LGPD establishes the legal hypotheses for the processing of personal data. In the WazzimaGiygg case:
hipotesesList: No consent from the data subject - The user did not authorize the processing of their data.
No legitimate interest of the controller - Persecution is not a legitimate interest.
Does not fit any legal hypothesis - The processing has no legal basis.
Deviation of purpose - Data was used for persecution, not for protection.
sub3_1Title: 3.1 Doxxing - Public Exposure of Personal Data
sub3_1Text1: Doxxing is the public exposure of an individual's personal data without their consent. In the WazzimaGiygg case:
doxxingList: Civil name exposed: "Pedro Henrique Cardona Peres" was publicly disclosed.
Location of exposure: Indexable public verification logs (CheckUser).
Consequence: Permanent SEO damage - second result on Google.
doxxingWarningText: The Wikipedia doxxing log appears as the second global result on Google for the name "Pedro Henrique Cardona Peres". This damage is permanent and irreversible, destroying the victim's professional and personal reputation.
sub3_2Text1: Device fingerprinting is the collection of information about the software and hardware of a device for persistent identification. In the WazzimaGiygg case:
fingerprintingList: IMEI: Unique 15-digit number of the mobile device.
MAC Address: Unique identifier of the network interface.
Use: Hardware monitoring beyond the permitted scope.
fingerprintingNoteText:
The collection of IMEI and MAC Address without authorization constitutes:

• LGPD violation (Arts. 6, 7) - processing without consent
• Device intrusion (Art. 154-A of the Penal Code) - hardware data collection
• Violation of the privacy policy of the Wikimedia Foundation
sub3_3Title: 3.3 Metadata Collection - Extraction of File Data
sub3_3Text1: Metadata is data about data - information such as date, time, location and camera used. In the WazzimaGiygg case:
metadataList: EXIF data: Metadata from photographs on Wikimedia Commons.
Use as "proof": Metadata used to track and persecute the user.
sub3_4Title: 3.4 Illegal Data Retention - Violation of the 90-Day Policy
sub3_4Text1: The global CheckUser policy establishes that IP data expires in 90 days. In the WazzimaGiygg case:
retencaoList: Access to logs older than 90 days: Linking of an account inactive for over 5 months.
Policy violation: Data that should have been deleted was accessed.
LGPD violation: Art. 46 - Security in data processing.
Evidence: Access to IP logs older than 150 days.
retencaoWarningTitle: ⚠️ ILLEGAL DATA RETENTION - GLOBAL POLICY VIOLATION:
retencaoWarningText: The global CheckUser policy establishes that IP data expires in 90 days. Access to logs older than 150 days proves violation of the data retention policy and constitutes an LGPD violation (Art. 46).
sub3_5Title: 3.5 Off-wiki Monitoring - Persecution Beyond the Platform
sub3_5Text1: Off-wiki monitoring is the tracking of activities of the user outside the platform. In the WazzimaGiygg case:
offwikiList: Photographs: Monitoring of contributions on Wikimedia Commons.

wmfResponsibilityText:
The Wikimedia Foundation, as data controller, has subsidiary responsibility for LGPD violations committed by its administrators and checkusers. The WMF can be held liable for:

• Not preventing unlawful data processing
• Not adequately supervising administrators
• Not removing defamatory content (Art. 19 of Marco Civil)
• Not ensuring LGPD compliance
victimConsequences: Permanent SEO damage: Permanent association with false accusations.
Reputation destruction: Professional and personal reputation destroyed.
Psychological damage: Anxiety, depression, feeling of persecution.
Professional damage: Loss of employment opportunities and clients.
Moral damage: Vexatious exposure and public humiliation.
platformConsequences: Legal liability: Possibility of fines and compensation.
Reputational damage: Loss of credibility as a free knowledge platform.
User loss: Collaborators withdraw for fear of privacy violations.
Trust crisis: The community loses trust in the platform.
Regulatory sanctions: Possibility of sanctions from ANPD.
section7Title: 7. 📢 Recommendations for Data Protection and Privacy
immediateActions: LGPD Take-down: Mandatory and definitive removal of Pedro Henrique Cardona Peres's personal data from all public logs.
De-indexation: Request to Google for removal of search results (right to be forgotten).
Notification to ANPD: Formal complaint to the National Data Protection Authority about LGPD violations.
Notification to WMF: Formal communication to the Wikimedia Foundation about privacy violations.
Demotion: Immediate removal of all involved agents from administrative positions.
structuralActions: Prohibition of Device Fingerprinting: Strict policy against hardware data collection.
Prohibition of Doxxing: Explicit policy with severe penalties.
LGPD Compliance: Implementation of privacy policies in compliance with the LGPD.
Strict Retention Policy: IP data deleted within 90 days.
Transparency: Publication of all verification actions with protection of sensitive data.
Privacy Audit: Periodic review of data processing practices.
userActions: Awareness: Know the risks of privacy violations.
Documentation: Record all evidence of privacy violations.
Reporting: Report privacy violations to ANPD and the Public Prosecutor's Office.
Legal Assistance: Consult lawyers specialized in digital law.
callToActionList: Criminal Investigation: Opening of police inquiry to investigate the crime of device intrusion (Art. 154-A of the Penal Code).
Civil Investigation: Civil action for moral and material damages against all agents involved.
Administrative Investigation: Inquiry at the Wikimedia Foundation to investigate LGPD violations.
Notification to ANPD: Formal complaint for LGPD violations.
Public Civil Action: Filing of public civil action for data protection of all users.
Structural Reform: Implementation of all proposed recommendations.
Whistleblower Protection: Guarantee that whistleblowers will not be persecuted.
finalText1: The WazzimaGiygg case reveals systemic privacy violations of the user, including doxxing, device fingerprinting, metadata collection, illegal data retention, off-wiki monitoring and multiple LGPD violations.
finalText2: The public exposure of the civil name "Pedro Henrique Cardona Peres" in indexable logs resulted in permanent SEO damage that destroyed his professional and personal reputation in an irreversible manner.
finalText3: The LGPD violations are serious and multiple, with penalties that can reach R$ 50 million per violation, in addition to compensation for moral and material damages.
finalText4: Privacy protection is a fundamental right that must be guaranteed to all users. The WazzimaGiygg case should serve as a warning and precedent for digital platforms to adopt effective measures for data protection and abuse prevention.
